description: Somos un colectivo de estudiantes de ingeniería que se encarga de desarrollar soluciones ingenieriles enfocadas en la aplicación de herramientas de IA , Automatización industrial y de análisis de datos para conformar diferentes soluciones integrales y multidisciplinarias
summary:
AgriNabla is an open-source agricultural intelligence platform that turns open environmental data into explainable farming decisions. We developed a web app that combines NASA POWER climate observations, Open-Meteo forecasts and ERA5 reanalysis, OpenTopography elevation models and FAOSTAT statistics on an interactive map. Users select a location and get climate analysis, terrain and soil insights, drought and frost risk screening, and crop rotation pathways. An AI assistant built on a Tri-RAG approach (semantic search, keyword search and a knowledge graph) grounds its answers in scientific evidence and the parcel’s own data, so every recommendation can be explained.

The platform addresses the challenge by making Earth observation data usable for farmers without field sensors, expensive subscriptions or technical expertise. It is important because small and medium producers face climate variability, water scarcity and soil degradation with little access to precision-agriculture tools. By relying on free APIs and open-source software, AgriNabla offers a scalable, transparent alternative that supports better planning, efficient use of water and inputs, and more sustainable farming.
details:
What it does and how it works

AgriNabla is an open agricultural intelligence and decision-support platform. A user selects a location on an interactive map, and the system retrieves and combines environmental data to produce:

  • Climate intelligence: monthly and historical climate from NASA POWER (solar radiation, temperature, wind, humidity, rainfall) plus forecasts and ERA5 reanalysis from Open-Meteo.
  • Terrain and soil insights: elevation models from OpenTopography (COP30, NASADEM, SRTM) to analyze slope, drainage and erosion risk.
  • Risk screening: early detection of drought, frost and water stress.
  • Crop rotation pathways: qualitative scenarios with the evidence and trade-offs behind each one.
  • An AI assistant that answers agronomic questions using the parcel’s own context.

The platform is built as decoupled services. The frontend handles maps and dashboards, the FastAPI backend centralizes calls to external providers and normalizes the data, and the AI engine produces explainable recommendations.

Explainable AI (Tri-RAG)

The assistant uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation design with three channels: dense semantic search over FAO manuals and scientific papers, sparse BM25 search for exact agronomic terminology, and reasoning over a knowledge graph of entity relations. A re-ranker merges the evidence with the parcel context (coordinates, soil, climate), and a language model produces recommendations grounded in sources instead of unsupported answers.

Benefits and intended impact

Precision agriculture is usually out of reach for small and medium producers because it requires IoT sensors and costly proprietary subscriptions. AgriNabla needs no field hardware and relies on free scientific APIs and satellite-derived data. Its intended impact is to help farmers, cooperatives, agronomists, researchers and public institutions to:

  • Plan rotations that are more resilient to climate variability
  • Use water and fertilizer more efficiently
  • Reduce soil erosion and improve soil health
  • Understand long-term climate trends in their territory

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, TailwindCSS, Zustand
  • Mapping and GIS: OpenLayers, Mapbox GL JS, Turf.js, Proj4, JSTS
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Spatial database: PostgreSQL with PostGIS
  • AI: Modal (serverless GPU) and vLLM serving open models such as Qwen or Llama
  • Data sources: NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, OpenTopography, FAOSTAT, Mapbox/OpenStreetMap, LibreTranslate

No special hardware is required.

What makes it creative

  • It turns scattered open Earth-observation datasets into a single, usable decision tool instead of another raw data portal.
  • It combines three retrieval methods so the AI is explainable rather than a black box.
  • It uses a serverless GPU design that scales with demand and drops to zero when idle, keeping costs low.
  • It is multilingual through LibreTranslate, which supports regional inclusion.

Factors our team considered

  • Accessibility and cost: open-source software and open APIs avoid licensing fees and vendor lock-in.
  • Transparency: when field or crop performance data is not available, the app shows rotation pathways as qualitative options and does not invent scores. We preferred honest limits over false precision.
  • Interoperability: support for open standards (GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, OGC) so it can integrate with other public or private systems.
  • Scalability: a modular architecture lets us add new data sources, models and dashboards without redesigning the system.
  • Future work: NDVI/NDWI indices through Google Earth Engine and Sentinel-2, an offline-capable mobile web app for low-connectivity areas, and multimodal AI for pest and disease detection from leaf photos.
